dublinCore.description: A sine-wave tone generator with a live FFT spectrum from 0 to 10 kHz on a decibel scale. Start/Stop the tone, set its frequency (20 Hz to 10 kHz) and amplitude (0 to 0.5) with sliders or by dragging across the plot, and watch the single spectral peak follow the tone.
relation: Chapter 2: Introduction to Signals and Systems
Chapter 7: DFT, FFT and Frequency Domain Analysis

learningObjectives: Identify the single spectral peak that a pure sine tone produces in the FFT display and read its frequency and level
Predict how the FFT peak moves along the frequency axis as the tone sweeps from low to high frequency, and relate its position to the pitch they hear
Explain how horizontal position on the plot maps linearly to a frequency between 20 Hz and 10 kHz
Calculate the peak level 20 log10(A) dB for an amplitude A and verify that halving A lowers the peak by about 6 dB
Explain why the read-out can differ from the set frequency by up to half a bin width (2.93 Hz at 48 kHz)
prerequisites: Sine waves: amplitude, frequency and period
Sound as a pressure wave; frequency and pitch

misconceptions.misconception: A louder tone has a higher frequency
misconceptions.correction: Amplitude and frequency are independent; amplitude changes the peak height, frequency moves it sideways
misconceptions.evidence: At 440 Hz, raising the amplitude from 0.10 to 0.40 lifts the peak from -20.0 dB to -8.0 dB while it stays at 439.5 Hz

misconceptions.misconception: Doubling the amplitude doubles the level in decibels
misconceptions.correction: Decibels are logarithmic: doubling the amplitude adds 20 log10(2) = 6.0 dB
misconceptions.evidence: At 1500 Hz the peak reads -20.0 dB at amplitude 0.10 and -14.0 dB at 0.20

misconceptions.misconception: The FFT measures the exact frequency of the tone
misconceptions.correction: The FFT measures at bins f_s/N apart, so the read-out is the nearest bin centre
misconceptions.evidence: A 1000 Hz tone reads 1002.0 Hz at 48 kHz, the centre of bin 171

accessibility.screenReaderScript: A sine-wave tone generator with its live FFT spectrum from 0 to 10 kHz. Press Start to hear the tone, then move the Frequency and Amplitude sliders, or drag across the plot, to move the single spectral peak and change its level in decibels.

controls.label: Start / Stop
controls.description: Starts audio on the first click, then fades the tone in and out; nothing plays until it is pressed

controls.label: Frequency
controls.description: Sets the oscillator frequency; dragging horizontally across the plot sets it to the frequency under the pointer

controls.label: Amplitude
controls.description: Sets the peak amplitude of the sine tone; the peak level is 20 log10(A) dB

visualElements.description: Magnitude spectrum (blue bars) from 0 to 10 kHz on a level axis from -80 to 0 dB; press and drag on it to set the frequency
Dashed line at the set frequency and a gold triangle on the strongest FFT bin
FFT peak frequency and level, PLAYING / STOPPED status, sample rate and bin width

model.description: A p5.sound oscillator produces x(t) = A sin(2 pi f t). The browser's analyser applies a Blackman window and an 8192-point FFT; the sketch plots each bin's level in dB relative to an amplitude-1 sine centred on a bin.
equations: x(t) = A sin(2 pi f t)
limitations: The read-out reports the centre of the strongest bin, so it can differ from the set frequency by up to half a bin (2.93 Hz at 48 kHz)
A tone between two bins reads up to about 1 dB low because of the Blackman window
Small speakers may not reproduce the lowest frequencies even though the FFT still shows the peak

instructionalStrategies: Worksheet table relating amplitude to level in decibels
Connecting pitch and octaves to peak position
extensions: Add a waveform selector (square, sawtooth, triangle) to reveal harmonics
Add a logarithmic frequency axis and compare it with musical pitch
